nodes.label: Falsified Claim: False-Positive Rate Bounded by HMAC Collision
nodes.rationale: FALSIFIED - never reintroduce. The original Canary Maze why-now asserted 'a canary sighting has a false-positive rate bounded by the collision probability of the HMAC, i.e. effectively zero'. reply.md states the correction verbatim: 'the earlier claim that false positives were bounded by HMAC collision was wrong', because a sighting does not establish two actors - intra-actor address rotation presents as a sighting. The tool may report only that a secret moved between request contexts; actor-distinctness is exactly the classifier problem it cannot escape.

nodes.label: Falsifying Measurement: 0 DOIs and 0 ISBNs Across 14,591 Revisions
nodes.rationale: The measurement that killed the fabricated-citation join, on the organizers' own dump: '0 DOIs, 0 ISBNs, 0 cite templates across all 14,591 revisions'. Three of the idea's four extractors had no input at all. Of the 69% of revisions carrying a bare URL, 8,473 URLs are shared by two or more accounts and the top hosts are wikiservice.at (2,412), jqp.vercel.app (1,523), api.datausa.io (1,017) plus markdown-scraping proxies - shared tooling, not shared sources. Never reintroduce a citation-resolution join on this corpus.

nodes.label: Falsified Fact: One Actor Label Spans 741 Addresses
nodes.rationale: From the organizers' own dump labels table: stored_revisions 899 against stored_revision_ips 741 and stored_revision_ip16 114 - one actor operating from 741 distinct addresses. Every change of address within a single actor would present as a different request context, so a sighting does not establish two actors. This fact is what falsified the HMAC-collision false-positive bound.

nodes.label: Shared-Tooling Join Lead
nodes.rationale: The live thread at hand-off: the critic's measurement surfaced a different join key in the organizers' own data - 8,473 URLs shared by 2+ accounts, dominated by markdown-scraping proxies (r.jina.ai, pure.md, md.succ.ai) - i.e. those agents shared tooling. On-theme, on a real agent wiki, on an ungated 4.2 MB download. Under validation and explicitly NOT a candidate until it passes - and it subsequently failed.

nodes.label: Batch Card wrong_brief Risk
nodes.rationale: Theme fit is the weakest in the set and the status is `unknown` pending an outsider test. The documented campaign is one human running six accounts with machine-generated payloads, not agents coordinating, so the write-up must say 'one operator, many accounts' and never 'swarm'. Compounding: maintainers did not ask for this - in GitHub's own discussion cross-repository detection 'wasn't a common theme' and 'No maintainers explicitly asked for batch-identifying labels' - and ~95% of the ground-truth campaign came from one account, leaving a ~25-submission multi-account tail.

nodes.label: Canary Maze Organic Sighting Dependency
nodes.rationale: The one genuine gamble in the set: an organic cross-context sighting may never fire in 31 hours. Mitigations: deploy domain, DNS and TLS first thing, make the seeded two-client replay the PRIMARY deliverable rather than a fallback, and paste minted URLs into public model products to produce third-party fetcher traffic in minutes. Also disclosed: tokens can be stripped, and minting for humans would be tracking.

nodes.label: Gate Verdict: 0 FAIL, 8 WARN
nodes.rationale: Disclosed at hand-off: all six criteria are `assumed` because no rubric is published; Batch Card's wrong_brief is `unknown` pending the outsider test; 11 research gaps. Isolation was structural - discovery ran in a subagent that never saw the event, its hosts, its sponsors or anything about the builder, and background was read only at Stage 10 after the ideas were final. Not checked: Socket's product pages (the biggest unchecked competitive risk), GitLab and Codeberg, Transluce's log distribution route, non-English wiki projects, Indeed and Upwork (both 403).

nodes.label: Non-Personalisation Disclosure
nodes.rationale: 'Not personalised: there is no background about you in this session - empty memory directory, no project CLAUDE.md, no repo history - so I can't tell you which of these is nearer your existing stack, and I won't guess.' The past-project check could not be run against real history either. Stated rather than guessed at.
